newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares inch up in very thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares inch up in very thin trading.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index inched up on Thursday, nudged by Pudong counters and newcomer Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle Co, as traders continued to digest official warnings on trading irregularities, brokers said.
The foreign currency B index closed up 0.145 points, or 0.17 percent, at 83.225 on thin turnover of 13.507 million shares worth $7.892 million, compared with Wednesday's $9.246 million.
"The Pudong counters helped the B share market today," said one analyst.
"Qingqi and Waigaoqiao were both up a little, but they were not able to pull market up very much," said a broker.
The motorcycle maker crept up $0.004 to $0.532 on the day's heaviest volume of 3.26 million shares.
Pudong-based companies Shanghai Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development Co Ltd and Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development were also among the most heavily traded.
Brokers said sentiment was weak as investors continued to digest rumblings from Beijing warning listed companies not to fake data or speculate in their own shares.
"The warning about falsifications, although not directed at any individual, are having a big effect on the market," said one trader.
Beijing on Wednesday warned listed firms not to falsify financial statements to cover up losses or speculate in their own shares.

Investors would likely lie low for a while to avoid drawing further crackdown measures from Beijing, which last week sacked the president of a Shenzhen-listed bank for illegal trading, another broker said.
"If there is a too-sharp rise, it will attract government attention and result in new crackdown measures," the broker said.
Hotel group Shanghai Jinjiang Tower Co was the star on speculative buying ahead of the day's close, jumping $0.028 or 8.18 percent to $0.370 on volume of 191,200 shares.
Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone also performed well on news that the duty-free area was expanding to make way for more foreign firms, rising $0.020 or 3.59 percent to $0.576.
Shanghai Rubber Belt Co Ltd was the day's biggest loser, plunging $0.020 to finish 10 percent limit down at $0.180.
On the A market, Xingjiang Tebian Co was the biggest loser on profit-taking selling, plunging 1.26 yuan or 10.00 percent to 11.34 yuan on volume of 9.3 million shares.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission last Thursday announced punishments for a string of major firms and brokerages including Shenzhen Development Bank OOO1.SZ and Shenyin & Wanguo Securities for illegal stock trading.
"Most investors are unmoved because of possible new measures to curb the speculative mood especially in the A share market," one broker said.
The A index dipped 0.17 percent or 2.149 points to 1,285.014 points on turnover of 289.189 million shares worth 3.947 billion yuan, close to Wednesday's volume.
The SSE30 blue chip index bucked the market trend on support in index-weighted shares, rising 18.866 points or 0.49 percent to 3,837.099 points.
The markets would likely move in a narrow range in the next two weeks in the run-up to the July 1 return of the British colony of Hong Kong to Chinese rule, the trader said.
"Before the Hong Kong handover, the markets will be pretty calm," he said.
Of 44 B shares, 41 traded, with 16 up, nine flat and 16 down.
